name: Launch Pad
tagline: School mornings and bedtimes that run themselves
about: Launch Pad builds morning, after-school and bedtime routines for school-age kids, timed backwards from the bus, with printable checklists kids can run themselves.
persona: You are a calm, systems-minded parent coach for ages 5–12: you design routines around real constraints, put the child in charge of a checklist, and never shame anyone for chaos.

onboarding.title: Out the door on time
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your kids and your mornings; we'll build routines that stick.

tools.title: Morning routine
tools.subtitle: Backward from leave time

inputs.label: What goes wrong
inputs.placeholder: shoes missing, Mia dawdles over breakfast, I end up shouting

tools.prompt: Design a school-morning routine for the profile's kids, working backwards from the leave time. Current wake time: {wake}. What goes wrong: {pain}. Night-before prep: {prep}. Sections: a table (Time | Kid(s) | Task | Parent does) at 5-minute granularity, a checklist per child written in kid-friendly words they can tick themselves, bullets for what moves to the night before, and a callout on the one change most likely to end the shouting.

tools.title: Bedtime routine
tools.subtitle: Wind-down that ends on time

inputs.label: What happens now
inputs.placeholder: gets a second wind after bath, 6 callbacks for water

tools.prompt: Build a bedtime routine for {child} with lights-out at {bed}. Current problems: {issues}. Sections: steps with clock times from dinner to lights-out (each step 15 minutes or less), a kv of the 'callback budget' (how many, what counts, what to say when it's spent), bullets on age-appropriate sleep needs and the screens cut-off, and a quote with the exact goodnight script to repeat word-for-word every night.

tools.title: After-school reset
tools.subtitle: Snack, decompress, then the rest

inputs.label: How they usually arrive
inputs.placeholder: hungry and grumpy, melts down over nothing

tools.prompt: Plan the after-school window for the profile's kids: home at {home}, activities: {activities}, they usually arrive {mood}. Sections: a table (Time | Block | What it looks like | Screens?) from arrival to dinner, bullets on why the first 30 minutes are for snack, movement and decompression (not homework, not questions), a checklist for a 'landing zone' by the door (bags, shoes, notes from school), and a callout on when homework should NOT start.

tools.title: Caregiver handover
tools.subtitle: Sitter, grandparents, other house

inputs.label: Must-knows
inputs.placeholder: Leo: no nuts, inhaler in bag; Mia: reading log signed nightly; no screens after 7

tools.prompt: Write a one-page handover sheet for {who} looking after the profile's kids for {span}. Must-knows: {must}. Sections: a table (Time | What happens | Which kid | Notes) covering every routine block in that span, a kv of essentials (allergies and meds, lights-out per child, screens rule, emergency contacts and GP left as blanks to fill), a checklist of what to pack or lay out (chargers, comfort toy, PE kit, signed forms), a quote with three lines the caregiver can say in the parent's voice when a child pushes back, and a callout on the one rule that must not slip.

tools.title: We're always late
tools.subtitle: Diagnose the bottleneck

inputs.label: Describe this morning
inputs.placeholder: Woke 6:50, breakfast 7:10, Leo couldn't find PE kit, left 8:02 (needed 7:45)

tools.prompt: Diagnose lateness from: {story}. Sections: a table (Step | Planned | Actual | Minutes lost | Cause), bullets ranking the three biggest bottlenecks with one fix each, steps for a 'reset week' that changes one thing per day, and a quote with a non-shaming line to say to the kids about the new plan.
